text: Introduction
title: Introduction

text: The epistle to the Ephesians is addressed to Christians who "are in danger of suffering from spiritual malnutrition,
title: Introduction

text: because they are not taking advantage of the enormous store of food and spiritual goods they have at their disposal.
title: Introduction

text: The epistle to the Ephesians has been called the believer's bank,
title: Introduction

text: the checkbook,
title: Introduction

text: the Bible's treasure room.
title: Introduction

text: This wonderful letter tells Christians about the great riches,
title: Introduction

text: the inheritance,
title: Introduction

text: and the fullness they possess in Jesus Christ and his church.
title: Introduction

text: It tells them what they possess and what they must do to appropriate it."
title: Introduction

text: (John MACARTHUR).
title: Introduction

text: This is not material wealth,
title: Introduction

text: but spiritual wealth.
title: Introduction

text: Ephesus was a very important city,
title: Introduction

text: one of the 5 key cities of the Roman Empire.
title: Introduction

text: It was definitely the largest city (apart from Rome) that Paul visited.
title: Introduction

text: It was so rich that it was called the "Bank of Asia".
title: Introduction

text: Traders came from all over to buy and sell their wares.
title: Introduction

text: And tourists visited to admire a temple dedicated to the goddess Artemis,
title: Introduction

text: one of the 7 wonders of the world at the time.
title: Introduction

text: With his letter,
title: Introduction

text: the apostle Paul certainly wanted to show the members of the church in Ephesus,
title: Introduction

text: surrounded by great material wealth,
title: Introduction

text: that the joy and contentment of a Christian is not based on the material.
title: Introduction

text: He wanted to remind them of the true riches we have in Christ,
title: Introduction

text: riches that don't spoil and that no one can steal!
title: Introduction

text: This theme is still relevant today.
title: Introduction

text: Today's world would have us believe that money brings happiness!
title: Introduction

text: But God's Word tells us that this is a lie.
title: Introduction

text: True,
title: Introduction

text: money can buy us things that make our daily lives easier,
title: Introduction

text: but money is powerless against the difficulties,
title: Introduction

text: suffering and great challenges of our life on earth.
title: Introduction

text: The key verse in Ephesians is right at the beginning:
title: Introduction

text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
title: Introduction

text: who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in heavenly places in Christ.
title: Introduction

text: Ephesians 1, 3
title: Introduction

text: In Jesus we have ALL spiritual blessing!
title: Introduction

text: And in the verses that follow,
title: Introduction

text: Paul gives us more details about these blessings.
title: Introduction

text: In the original Greek version of the Bible,
title: Introduction

text: verses 3 to 14 of the first chapter of Ephesians are a single sentence!
title: Introduction

text: According to Paul,
title: Introduction

text: the list of spiritual riches for those "in Christ" is long:
title: Introduction

text: election and predestination;
title: Introduction

text: adoption;
title: Introduction

text: love;
title: Introduction

text: redemption;
title: Introduction

text: forgiveness;
title: Introduction

text: grace;
title: Introduction

text: wisdom and understanding;
title: Introduction

text: inheritance;
title: Introduction

text: the Holy Spirit;
title: Introduction

text: power;
title: Introduction

text: hope and the church.
title: Introduction

text: In the next few pages,
title: Introduction

text: we will study these biblical truths,
title: Introduction

text: but not simply as doctrines or knowledge for our heads.
title: Introduction

text: Instead,
title: Introduction

text: we'll be looking to discover how they can become real riches for our daily lives with everyday actions.
title: Introduction

text: Election
title: Introduction

text: We are chosen by God,
title: Introduction

text: before the foundation of the world,
title: Introduction

text: in Christ,
title: Introduction

text: to be holy (Ephesians 1, 4).
title: Introduction

text: What is election?
title: Introduction

text: Election is a difficult doctrine to understand.
title: Introduction

text: It's important not to get hung up on why some have been elected and others have not.
title: Introduction

text: God's sovereignty means that we could never understand all his actions.
title: Introduction

text: What's important to remember about this doctrine:
title: Introduction

text: - Salvation begins with God.
title: Introduction

text: He took the initiative to save man.
title: Introduction

text: We are so corrupted by sin that it is impossible for us to take the first step.
title: Introduction

text: - This is an action that God does alone and for himself.
title: Introduction

text: - He does not use the same criteria as our world in his choices (1 Corinthians 1, 26 to 29).
title: Introduction

text: - God's election has a purpose.
title: Introduction

text: He has chosen us to glorify him,
title: Introduction

text: to serve him and to do good works.
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make election a richness in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Thank God every day that you are one of His chosen ones.
title: Introduction

text: Ask for his help to live worthy of one of God's chosen.
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read 1 Corinthians 1, 26 to 31.
title: Introduction

text: These verses teach us that God does not choose as the world chooses.
title: Introduction

text: What are his criteria for choice?
title: Introduction

text: Just because God doesn't choose what's "strong" doesn't mean he doesn't consider us.
title: Introduction

text: Read Isaiah 43, 4 and memorize it.
title: Introduction

text: - Personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: Do you feel that others - your husband or wife,
title: Introduction

text: your superiors or colleagues,
title: Introduction

text: the members of your church - don't consider you?
title: Introduction

text: Remember that you are one of God's "chosen ones".
title: Introduction

text: You're very important to God.
title: Introduction

text: He considers you.
title: Introduction

text: You are precious in His eyes.
title: Introduction

text: Your importance is not based on your diplomas,
title: Introduction

text: your social position or your material possessions,
title: Introduction

text: but it's simply by grace that God has chosen you.
title: Introduction

text: If you're careful,
title: Introduction

text: you'll notice it in your everyday life!
title: Introduction

text: - Towards others:
title: Introduction

text: Treat your spiritual brothers and sisters,
title: Introduction

text: who are also God's chosen ones,
title: Introduction

text: with respect and love!
title: Introduction

text: Don't despise those who are weak.
title: Introduction

text: Rather,
title: Introduction

text: show them that they are precious in the eyes of God and the church.
title: Introduction

text: Predestination
title: Introduction

text: In his love,
title: Introduction

text: God predestined us to be his adopted children through Jesus Christ (Ephesians 1, 5).
title: Introduction

text: What is predestination?
title: Introduction

text: Predestination is linked to election.
title: Introduction

text: While election is more about the past,
title: Introduction

text: what has happened,
title: Introduction

text: what we already know (we are God's chosen ones),
title: Introduction

text: predestination is about the future,
title: Introduction

text: what God has ordained for our lives.
title: Introduction

text: The word translated "predestine" in the Word of God comes from the Greek word "proorizo",
title: Introduction

text: meaning "to determine beforehand",
title: Introduction

text: "to order",
title: Introduction

text: "to decide in advance".
title: Introduction

text: Like election,
title: Introduction

text: predestination is not easy to understand.
title: Introduction

text: To predestine means to fix one's destiny in advance.
title: Introduction

text: We,
title: Introduction

text: God's elect,
title: Introduction

text: are predestined to become children of God.
title: Introduction

text: Predestination emphasizes that God has chosen us for something.
title: Introduction

text: God has a plan for the life of each of his children.
title: Introduction

text: He has planned everything in advance.
title: Introduction

text: I don't have to worry.
title: Introduction

text: God is in control of my future.
title: Introduction

text: And his plans for my life are very good plans.
title: Introduction

text: Much better than I can imagine.
title: Introduction

text: Missing out on God's plan for my life doesn't mean that God will abandon me or that I'll lose my salvation,
title: Introduction

text: but I may miss out on God's great blessings.
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make predestination a richness in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Before you pray,
title: Introduction

text: write down everything you'd like to do - short and long term - on a piece of paper.
title: Introduction

text: Place everything in God's hands.
title: Introduction

text: Ask him to show you if your plans are also HIS plans.
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read Psalm 139.
title: Introduction

text: What does this Psalm teach you about God's relationship with you and His future plans for you?
title: Introduction

text: - personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: Examine your heart.
title: Introduction

text: Does all your happiness depend on the success of your plans?
title: Introduction

text: Remember that God may have another plan for your life.
title: Introduction

text: Do you trust God with your future?
title: Introduction

text: Do worries keep you awake at night and unable to work during the day?
title: Introduction

text: Will you be ready to abandon one of your plans if God shows you another way?
title: Introduction

text: - towards others:
title: Introduction

text: If you're not sure what God's will is for you,
title: Introduction

text: ask a brother or sister in Christ for advice.
title: Introduction

text: Also,
title: Introduction

text: seek help for those who have to make important decisions about their future.
title: Introduction

text: Adoption
title: Introduction

text: In his love,
title: Introduction

text: God has predestined us to be his adopted children through Jesus Christ (Ephesians 1.5).
title: Introduction

text: What is adoption?
title: Introduction

text: In the time of the apostle Paul,
title: Introduction

text: childless couples frequently adopted a son who became their heir.
title: Introduction

text: Even if the adoptive son's biological parents were still alive,
title: Introduction

text: they no longer had any rights over him once the adoption was completed.
title: Introduction

text: Plenary adoption is a legal act.
title: Introduction

text: The child does not simply change the family.
title: Introduction

text: There is a complete break with the old family.
title: Introduction

text: The adopted child changes his or her name and receives a new birth certificate.
title: Introduction

text: He or she is no longer entitled to inheritance from his or her biological family,
title: Introduction

text: but is fully integrated into the lineage of his or her new family.
title: Introduction

text: The old family no longer has any rights over him or her.
title: Introduction

text: In some countries,
title: Introduction

text: biological parents no longer even have the right to see their child.
title: Introduction

text: Paul uses this social custom to teach the following biblical truths:
title: Introduction

text: - We are chosen before we are born,
title: Introduction

text: but we become God's children by adoption the moment we accept God's salvation.
title: Introduction

text: - We are fully children of God.
title: Introduction

text: The break with the past is complete.
title: Introduction

text: Our "old family" no longer has any power over us.
title: Introduction

text: - Adoption was made possible by Christ's death.
title: Introduction

text: It took place the moment we believed and became members of God's family (Romans 8, 15),
title: Introduction

text: but it will be fully realized when we put on our resurrection body (Romans 8, 23).
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make adoption a richness in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Thank God for your new spiritual family.
title: Introduction

text: Speak the names of those who have become true fathers and mothers,
title: Introduction

text: brothers and sisters in the church for you.
title: Introduction

text: Thank God for them.
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read Ephesians 4, 17 to 32.
title: Introduction

text: Make a first list of behaviors from the old family that are no longer allowed in the new family,
title: Introduction

text: the family of God.
title: Introduction

text: Then make a second list of behaviors you must learn as sons and daughters of God's family.
title: Introduction

text: - Personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: Examine your life to see if you still have any of the behaviors of your old life.
title: Introduction

text: If so,
title: Introduction

text: seek to change them,
title: Introduction

text: with the help of the Holy Spirit.
title: Introduction

text: - towards others:
title: Introduction

text: Ask God to show you who in your church needs a spiritual father or mother or brother or sister.
title: Introduction

text: Draw close to that person and accompany him or her in life as you would a brother or sister in your natural family.
title: Introduction

text: Love
title: Introduction

text: God loves us and has always wanted us to become his sons through Jesus Christ (Ephesians 1, 4 to 5).
title: Introduction

text: What is God's love?
title: Introduction

text: God's love is perfect,
title: Introduction

text: infinite and pure.
title: Introduction

text: It's not just a feeling.
title: Introduction

text: God showed his love for us in a very,
title: Introduction

text: very important act:
title: Introduction

text: he gave his only son to save us (John 3, 16).
title: Introduction

text: - God's love is unconditional:
title: Introduction

text: he doesn't ask me to improve my life before he saves me!
title: Introduction

text: The unconditional nature of God's love never changes.
title: Introduction

text: God continues to love us,
title: Introduction

text: even if we fall into sin,
title: Introduction

text: even if we abandon him.
title: Introduction

text: His love for us remains the same.
title: Introduction

text: It doesn't diminish.
title: Introduction

text: - God's love is selfless,
title: Introduction

text: that is,
title: Introduction

text: it's focused on us.
title: Introduction

text: In giving his son,
title: Introduction

text: he didn't think of himself,
title: Introduction

text: but of us!
title: Introduction

text: And he continues to help us,
title: Introduction

text: to be of service to us.
title: Introduction

text: - God's love is enormous:
title: Introduction

text: God loves us so much that he gave his most precious gift,
title: Introduction

text: his only son.
title: Introduction

text: There's nothing greater he could have done for us.
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make God's love a richness in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Thank God every day for his love for you.
title: Introduction

text: Pay attention to the little signs of God's love during the day.
title: Introduction

text: At the end of the day,
title: Introduction

text: write down the events that show God's love for you in a notebook and thank him.
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read Ephesians 3, 17 to 19.
title: Introduction

text: - personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: In this passage,
title: Introduction

text: the apostle Paul uses 2 images to encourage his readers to enjoy God's love:
title: Introduction

text: - take root in this love:
title: Introduction

text: just as a tree spreads its roots in the earth so as not to be blown away by the wind and to find nourishment...
title: Introduction

text: - build on this love:
title: Introduction

text: God's love is a solid foundation,
title: Introduction

text: enabling us to build and move forward in our spiritual life.
title: Introduction

text: Think about how these 2 images can help you live and experience God's love in everyday life.
title: Introduction

text: - Towards others:
title: Introduction

text: Share your testimony about God's love in your life with your friends,
title: Introduction

text: your wife or husband or the brothers and sisters in your church.
title: Introduction

text: And show them through your actions that God loves them.
title: Introduction

text: Redemption
title: Introduction

text: In Jesus we have redemption through his blood (Ephesians 1, 7).
title: Introduction

text: What is redemption?
title: Introduction

text: The word "redemption" is part of a set of terms that describe salvation.
title: Introduction

text: Literally,
title: Introduction

text: it means "to untie far off",
title: Introduction

text: "deliverance".
title: Introduction

text: It evokes the notion of redemption,
title: Introduction

text: like a slave,
title: Introduction

text: bound to a master,
title: Introduction

text: and freed by the payment of a sum of money.
title: Introduction

text: Man is a slave to sin and its consequences,
title: Introduction

text: that is death.
title: Introduction

text: Redemption frees him from the power of sin and its legal consequences.
title: Introduction

text: In His work of redemption,
title: Introduction

text: Christ paid the price of redemption for all mankind.
title: Introduction

text: The price is clearly indicated as to its nature:
title: Introduction

text: it is the blood of Christ.
title: Introduction

text: Since we have been redeemed at this price,
title: Introduction

text: we must serve him who paid it (1 Corinthians 7, 22 to 23).
title: Introduction

text: Redemption can be summed up in three basic ideas:
title: Introduction

text: (1) human beings are redeemed from something,
title: Introduction

text: namely the slavery of sin;
title: Introduction

text: (2) they are redeemed by something,
title: Introduction

text: through the payment of a price,
title: Introduction

text: namely the blood of Christ;
title: Introduction

text: (3) they are redeemed for something,
title: Introduction

text: namely to be free.
title: Introduction

text: Once set free,
title: Introduction

text: they are invited to make themselves slaves of the Lord who redeemed them.
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make salvation or redemption a richness in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: In your daily prayer,
title: Introduction

text: you can thank God for saving you from sin,
title: Introduction

text: death,
title: Introduction

text: debauchery...
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: regularly read the accounts of Jesus' death,
title: Introduction

text: for example Luke 23, 33 to 49.
title: Introduction

text: Imagine yourself in the crowd watching the crucifixion.
title: Introduction

text: Remind yourself of Jesus' enormous sacrifice.
title: Introduction

text: - Personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: You have benefited from the redemption of his son Jesus.
title: Introduction

text: He has freed you from Satan's slavery.
title: Introduction

text: But are you really free?
title: Introduction

text: Examine your life with the help of the Holy Spirit to find out if you're still a "slave" to Satan.
title: Introduction

text: Do you still have bad habits that don't glorify God?
title: Introduction

text: - towards others:
title: Introduction

text: Salvation becomes even more precious when shared with others.
title: Introduction

text: Announce Jesus' salvation at least once a week to someone who doesn't yet know him.
title: Introduction

text: Forgiveness
title: Introduction

text: In Jesus we have the forgiveness of sins (Ephesians 1, 7).
title: Introduction

text: What is forgiveness?
title: Introduction

text: The word "forgive" means to erase everything,
title: Introduction

text: to wipe the slate clean,
title: Introduction

text: to give grace,
title: Introduction

text: to cancel a debt.
title: Introduction

text: Forgiveness is not granted because a guilty person deserves to be forgiven.
title: Introduction

text: Forgiveness is a decision not to hold a grudge against someone,
title: Introduction

text: despite what they have done.
title: Introduction

text: No one deserves to be forgiven.
title: Introduction

text: Forgiveness is an act of love,
title: Introduction

text: mercy and grace.
title: Introduction

text: The Bible tells us that we all need God's forgiveness.
title: Introduction

text: We have all committed sins (1 John 1, 8).
title: Introduction

text: Every sin is essentially an act of rebellion against God and ruins my relationship with him.
title: Introduction

text: And only his forgiveness can restore that relationship.
title: Introduction

text: God's forgiveness cannot be earned through good works.
title: Introduction

text: You can't buy God's forgiveness.
title: Introduction

text: You can only receive it,
title: Introduction

text: by faith,
title: Introduction

text: because of God's grace and mercy.
title: Introduction

text: All you have to do is ask God to forgive you through Jesus,
title: Introduction

text: believing that Jesus died,
title: Introduction

text: to offer you this forgiveness - and God will forgive you.
title: Introduction

text: God's forgiveness is total.
title: Introduction

text: Once granted,
title: Introduction

text: the sin that broke my relationship with God no longer exists before him.
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make forgiveness a richness in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Ask the Holy Spirit to show you if there are any sins in your life.
title: Introduction

text: If you find any,
title: Introduction

text: ask God's forgiveness in Jesus.
title: Introduction

text: Thank God for his forgiveness.
title: Introduction

text: If you're still troubled by an old sin for which you've already asked forgiveness,
title: Introduction

text: ask God to remove it from your mind.
title: Introduction

text: -Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read 1 John chapter 1, 8 to chapter 2, 2.
title: Introduction

text: Try to express in your own words what the apostle John is saying here about the forgiveness of our sins.
title: Introduction

text: - Personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: Be careful not to abuse God's forgiveness.
title: Introduction

text: Don't say "It's all right,
title: Introduction

text: God will forgive me".
title: Introduction

text: This attitude shows that you're mocking God,
title: Introduction

text: and God hates that.
title: Introduction

text: - Towards others:
title: Introduction

text: Visit those who have fallen into sin and are overwhelmed by what has happened.
title: Introduction

text: Encourage them with God's promises,
title: Introduction

text: support them in prayer.
title: Introduction

text: Grace
title: Introduction

text: In him we have redemption through his blood,
title: Introduction

text: the forgiveness of sins,
title: Introduction

text: according to the riches of his grace (Ephesians 1, 4 to 5).
title: Introduction

text: What is God's grace?
title: Introduction

text: Grace means receiving God's salvation completely apart from any merit or act on our part.
title: Introduction

text: God has done everything in Jesus' name for us.
title: Introduction

text: Salvation is a gift,
title: Introduction

text: not a reward.
title: Introduction

text: Salvation is God's work,
title: Introduction

text: a finished work;
title: Introduction

text: we can neither add to it nor take away from it.
title: Introduction

text: We are saved by grace (Ephesians 2, 5 and verses 8 to 9),
title: Introduction

text: AND we live and serve by grace (Ephesians 3, 2 and verses 7 to 8).
title: Introduction

text: God's grace doesn't stop at salvation,
title: Introduction

text: but continues to work in our everyday lives.
title: Introduction

text: God's blessings in our lives are not rewards for our obedience,
title: Introduction

text: good works or active participation in church life.
title: Introduction

text: God blesses us by pure grace.
title: Introduction

text: Obedience to God and good works have an important place in our lives.
title: Introduction

text: BUT if I act while thinking in my heart only of what I can "win" with God,
title: Introduction

text: I'm on the wrong track.
title: Introduction

text: The motivation God is looking for is to please Him.
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make grace a richness in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Make a list of everything God has given you by pure grace,
title: Introduction

text: without you deserving it.
title: Introduction

text: Thank God for everything on the list.
title: Introduction

text: Make a second list of everything you'd like to have or do.
title: Introduction

text: Give the list to God.
title: Introduction

text: Tell him you don't deserve any of these things,
title: Introduction

text: but you're counting on his grace!
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read 1 Corinthians 15, 8 to 10 and 2 Corinthians 12, 8 to 10 and discover how the apostle Paul experienced God's grace in his life.
title: Introduction

text: - personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: We're influenced by our world,
title: Introduction

text: which tells us "You deserve this because you did that",
title: Introduction

text: "You're good because you're qualified"...
title: Introduction

text: BUT God tells us "Everything you have I gave you.
title: Introduction

text: You didn't do anything to deserve it.
title: Introduction

text: I didn't give you this job because you're qualified,
title: Introduction

text: but because I love you."
title: Introduction

text: Think about whether you're really living fully on God's grace.
title: Introduction

text: Are you obeying God to please him or to gain something from him?
title: Introduction

text: - towards others:
title: Introduction

text: Share this meaning of God's grace with brothers and sisters who are discouraged because they failed an exam or missed out on something they longed for.
title: Introduction

text: Wisdom and intelligence
title: Introduction

text: Yes,
title: Introduction

text: God has showered us with his blessings.
title: Introduction

text: He has given us all wisdom and understanding.
title: Introduction

text: (Ephesians 1, 8).
title: Introduction

text: What are wisdom and understanding?
title: Introduction

text: The basis of wisdom and intelligence is knowledge,
title: Introduction

text: that is an accumulation of information obtained through education or experience.
title: Introduction

text: There are those who confuse knowledge,
title: Introduction

text: intelligence and wisdom.
title: Introduction

text: They think that knowledge automatically leads to intelligence and even wisdom.
title: Introduction

text: But to be considered intelligent,
title: Introduction

text: it's not enough just to accumulate knowledge;
title: Introduction

text: you also have to understand it and know how to use it.
title: Introduction

text: That's intelligence.
title: Introduction

text: Wisdom goes even further.
title: Introduction

text: To be wise means to have the discernment when and how to apply the knowledge you have acquired,
title: Introduction

text: and to be able to pass on your knowledge and discernment to others.
title: Introduction

text: The Word of God teaches us that God can and will give us intelligence and wisdom BUT with the aim of knowing him,
title: Introduction

text: the living God,
title: Introduction

text: of knowing his plan of salvation and the riches he has reserved for us (see also Ephesians 1, 17 to 20).
title: Introduction

text: Actions to turn wisdom and intelligence into riches in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Thank God for the wisdom and understanding he has already given you.
title: Introduction

text: Ask him to show you how to use the knowledge you've gained in Bible school,
title: Introduction

text: church,
title: Introduction

text: conferences and personal study for his glory.
title: Introduction

text: Ask God to increase your intelligence so that you can better understand his Word and pass on your knowledge to others.
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read 1 Corinthians 1, 18 to 25.
title: Introduction

text: These words from the apostle Paul remind us that God's wisdom is different from that of our world.
title: Introduction

text: - personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: Intelligence and wisdom are highly regarded and sought after in our world.
title: Introduction

text: But BEWARE:
title: Introduction

text: it's not the same as with God.
title: Introduction

text: Examine your heart with the help of the Holy Spirit to discover what motivates you in your quest to expand your knowledge.
title: Introduction

text: Remember that God wants you to seek first to know him.
title: Introduction

text: - Toward others:
title: Introduction

text: Reflect on what you've learned in the last few weeks at church or during other teachings.
title: Introduction

text: Write down an important lesson that has made a difference in your life and share it with a family member or friend.
title: Introduction

text: Inheritance
title: Introduction

text: In Christ we have also become heirs...
title: Introduction

text: (Ephesians 1, 11).
title: Introduction

text: What is a Christian inheritance?
title: Introduction

text: It's the property left by a deceased person to those still living,
title: Introduction

text: usually family members.
title: Introduction

text: According to the Word of God,
title: Introduction

text: God has an inheritance for us,
title: Introduction

text: his children.
title: Introduction

text: It is the salvation brought by Jesus Christ that entitles us to this inheritance.
title: Introduction

text: Everything we study in this booklet is part of that inheritance.
title: Introduction

text: Paul calls it an inheritance of "glorious riches" (Ephesians 1, 18).
title: Introduction

text: Being heirs means that we are not yet in full possession of these riches.
title: Introduction

text: But if we live with God,
title: Introduction

text: if Jesus and the Holy Spirit dwell within us,
title: Introduction

text: we can already taste the riches of our heavenly Father.
title: Introduction

text: Just as a child who lives in the bosom of his family can already enjoy his father's possessions to some extent.
title: Introduction

text: And our full acquisition of the heavenly inheritance is promised by the Holy Spirit (see next chapter).
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make the inheritance a richness in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Thank God for the riches he has given you.
title: Introduction

text: List them one by one.
title: Introduction

text: Ask God to help you make better use of them.
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read Ephesians 1 and make a list of all your spiritual blessings.
title: Introduction

text: - personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: Are there times when you feel poor?
title: Introduction

text: Are you jealous of others who seem to have more than you?
title: Introduction

text: Remember that God's riches are at your disposal.
title: Introduction

text: Remember that these are riches that no one can steal and that do not spoil.
title: Introduction

text: At the end of the day,
title: Introduction

text: take time to reflect on which of the riches in Ephesians 1 you were able to use throughout the day.
title: Introduction

text: Start a little notebook and write down God's blessings every day.
title: Introduction

text: - to others:
title: Introduction

text: God wants us to share our spiritual heritage with our family and our brothers and sisters in Christ.
title: Introduction

text: Every morning,
title: Introduction

text: choose one of the riches of your inheritance and find a way to "give" it to someone you meet during the day.

text: The Holy Spirit
title: Introduction

text: In Christ also you who have believed have received from God the Holy Spirit,
title: Introduction

text: whom he promised and by whom he sealed you to belong to him.
title: Introduction

text: (Ephesians 1, 13)
title: Introduction

text: What does it mean to be sealed with the Holy Spirit?
title: Introduction

text: Among the Jews,
title: Introduction

text: the seal marked the end of a transaction:
title: Introduction

text: when the agreement had been reached,
title: Introduction

text: the deed done and the price paid,
title: Introduction

text: the seal was affixed to the contract to make it definitive.
title: Introduction

text: A seal is an imprint designed to guarantee the authenticity of a document or piece of information,
title: Introduction

text: and to show whether the contents have been altered or damaged.
title: Introduction

text: - A seal establishes the owner's rights and identifies his or her property.
title: Introduction

text: The Holy Spirit thus becomes the divine imprint on us.
title: Introduction

text: We are God's property.
title: Introduction

text: - A seal indicates that it is a genuine work,
title: Introduction

text: a completed and non-negotiable transaction,
title: Introduction

text: bearing the seal of God.
title: Introduction

text: - A seal indicates that it is an authentic work,
title: Introduction

text: a completed and non-negotiable transaction,
title: Introduction

text: bearing the stamp of the competent authority.
title: Introduction

text: The work of salvation is perfect and can no longer be doubted.
title: Introduction

text: - Those who carry a document sealed with a seal are under the protection of the owner of the seal.
title: Introduction

text: God is our protector.
title: Introduction

text: He ensures our security.
title: Introduction

text: The Holy Spirit also acts as the guarantor or pledge of our inheritance.
title: Introduction

text: Whoever pays a pledge,
title: Introduction

text: makes a firm commitment to the other to give it all later.
title: Introduction

text: The Holy Spirit assures us of the totality of our inheritance.
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make the Holy Spirit a richness in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Thank God for the gift of the Holy Spirit.
title: Introduction

text: Ask for the Holy Spirit to fill you completely,
title: Introduction

text: so that you can listen to His voice.
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read the Gospel of John 15, 7 to 15.
title: Introduction

text: What do these verses teach you about the Holy Spirit?
title: Introduction

text: - personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: Is the mark of the Holy Spirit really visible in your life?
title: Introduction

text: Can everyone see that you belong to God?
title: Introduction

text: Ask the Holy Spirit to show you what's wrong with you,
title: Introduction

text: and to transform you into the image of the living God.
title: Introduction

text: - towards others:
title: Introduction

text: Get to know your spiritual gifts,
title: Introduction

text: and start exercising them for the good of your brothers and sisters in Christ.

text: Hope
title: Introduction

text: So that you may know the hope he gave you when he called you (Ephesians 1, 18).
title: Introduction

text: What is Christian hope?
title: Introduction

text: To hope is to firmly believe that a desire will soon be fulfilled.
title: Introduction

text: Christian hope is the expectation of the fulfillment of God's promises.
title: Introduction

text: Hope concerns all God's promises,
title: Introduction

text: but especially those concerning our life after death,
title: Introduction

text: in the presence of God and Jesus,
title: Introduction

text: the return of Jesus,
title: Introduction

text: the new earth and the new heaven.
title: Introduction

text: To hope means that it hasn't yet "happened",
title: Introduction

text: but to believe with certainty that our expectations will be fulfilled.
title: Introduction

text: Such hope can have a profound influence on our lives.
title: Introduction

text: Instead of sinking into fear and anxiety,
title: Introduction

text: we can live in joy and peace.
title: Introduction

text: But we mustn't forget that the basis of our hope must be solid and reliable.
title: Introduction

text: If our hope is founded on other human beings or other forces than the living God,
title: Introduction

text: we are bound to be disappointed.
title: Introduction

text: Only a hope founded on God,
title: Introduction

text: on his Son Jesus and on the Holy Spirit guarantees the fulfillment of the promises awaited.
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make hope a richness in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Thank God for his promises and the hope we have in him.
title: Introduction

text: Put your fears and worries in His hands.
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read the following verses and choose one to memorize:
title: Introduction

text: John 10, 28;
title: Introduction

text: Ephesians 3, 20 to 21;
title: Introduction

text: Revelation 21, 4.
title: Introduction

text: - Personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: Do you constantly worry?
title: Introduction

text: Do you live in fear that something bad might happen in your life or the lives of your loved ones?
title: Introduction

text: There are many biblical examples of how God keeps his promises:
title: Introduction

text: Abraham and Sarah,
title: Introduction

text: Jacob,
title: Introduction

text: Joseph,
title: Introduction

text: Ruth,
title: Introduction

text: Nehemiah...
title: Introduction

text: Study one of these characters,
title: Introduction

text: paying attention to how God accompanied this person,
title: Introduction

text: especially during difficult times.
title: Introduction

text: - To others:
title: Introduction

text: Make a pretty card with an encouraging Bible verse and give it to a friend in need.
title: Introduction

text: You can also send the verse by SMS,
title: Introduction

text: WhatsApp or other means.

text: The power
title: Introduction

text: You will know the extraordinary power God has shown for us who believe in him (Ephesians 1, 19).
title: Introduction

text: What is the power of God?
title: Introduction

text: A power is a means or a strength that enables you to do great things or to dominate over other people or things.
title: Introduction

text: It is much sought-after in our world.
title: Introduction

text: WARNING:
title: Introduction

text: when the Bible speaks of the power of God,
title: Introduction

text: it's not the same thing.
title: Introduction

text: Firstly,
title: Introduction

text: God's power is greater than anything we can imagine.
title: Introduction

text: He is the creator of our world and has power over the life and death of everything that exists.
title: Introduction

text: Secondly,
title: Introduction

text: he uses his power for good,
title: Introduction

text: not for evil,
title: Introduction

text: as is the case in our world.
title: Introduction

text: God showed his power in the death and resurrection of his son Jesus,
title: Introduction

text: who brought us salvation.
title: Introduction

text: This power is also shown in the ascension and exaltation of Jesus and in his supreme position over the church.
title: Introduction

text: It is this power that is available to us.
title: Introduction

text: Unlimited,
title: Introduction

text: unimaginable power,
title: Introduction

text: but always with the aim of saving,
title: Introduction

text: not destroying!
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make power a richness in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Thank God for his acts in the past which have shown that he is all-powerful and which are still visible today,
title: Introduction

text: for example the creation of the world,
title: Introduction

text: your creation,
title: Introduction

text: the death and resurrection of Jesus...
title: Introduction

text: (Complete the list yourself).
title: Introduction

text: If you find yourself in a situation or facing a problem that seems impossible,
title: Introduction

text: tell yourself that nothing is impossible for the living God,
title: Introduction

text: and entrust the situation into his hands.
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read Isaiah 40, 18 to 31.
title: Introduction

text: What do these verses teach you about God's omnipotence?
title: Introduction

text: - personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: Do you really rely on God's power in your everyday life?
title: Introduction

text: Or is it your own efforts and strength that you're looking for?
title: Introduction

text: Are you seeking God's power for YOURSELF,
title: Introduction

text: to glorify yourself,
title: Introduction

text: to seek advancement for yourself and your family alone,
title: Introduction

text: or to help and save others?
title: Introduction

text: - towards others:
title: Introduction

text: Examine your relationships with others to see if you're really using the power God has given you for their good.

text: The church
title: Introduction

text: He put all things under his feet,
title: Introduction

text: and gave him as supreme head to the church,
title: Introduction

text: which is his body,
title: Introduction

text: the fullness of him who fills all in all.
title: Introduction

text: (Ephesians 1, 22 to 23).
title: Introduction

text: The apostle Paul used several images to explain what the church is.
title: Introduction

text: In our passage,
title: Introduction

text: Ephesians chapter 1,
title: Introduction

text: he speaks of the body of Christ (see also 1 Corinthians 12),
title: Introduction

text: and in the same epistle chapter 3, 19 to 22,
title: Introduction

text: he uses the image of a people,
title: Introduction

text: a family and a house.
title: Introduction

text: What is the church,
title: Introduction

text: the body of Christ?
title: Introduction

text: Christ is the head.
title: Introduction

text: The head is the most important part of the body.
title: Introduction

text: It's in the head that the brain is located,
title: Introduction

text: where all information,
title: Introduction

text: thoughts and decisions are concentrated.
title: Introduction

text: It's where intelligence,
title: Introduction

text: willpower and memory are stored.
title: Introduction

text: All the organs and limbs of our body are under the control of our brain.
title: Introduction

text: If we say that Christ is the head of the Church,
title: Introduction

text: we understand that all its members depend on HIM.
title: Introduction

text: The image of the body also underlines the unity of the church,
title: Introduction

text: the complementarity of its members and the solidarity that must reign between them.
title: Introduction

text: What is the church,
title: Introduction

text: God's family?
title: Introduction

text: When we become Christians,
title: Introduction

text: we also become members of a new family.
title: Introduction

text: With this image,
title: Introduction

text: the apostle Paul drew inspiration from the Jewish family,
title: Introduction

text: where each member had a fixed place with tasks and obligations.
title: Introduction

text: It's the same in the church,
title: Introduction

text: where each member has a role to play according to his or her gifts.
title: Introduction

text: Two other important characteristics of the Jewish family were fruitfulness and solidarity.
title: Introduction

text: Fruitfulness in the church means enlarging it by winning new converts!
title: Introduction

text: Solidarity means helping each other in times of need.
title: Introduction

text: What is the church,
title: Introduction

text: a house,
title: Introduction

text: a building?
title: Introduction

text: This image underlines the importance of the foundation (Jesus Christ) and the fact that the church is "under construction",
title: Introduction

text: not yet finished.
title: Introduction

text: Actions to make the church an asset in your life:
title: Introduction

text: - Prayer:
title: Introduction

text: Thank God for his church in your country,
title: Introduction

text: with all its weaknesses and shortcomings.
title: Introduction

text: - Bible reading:
title: Introduction

text: Read Ephesians 2, 13 to 22 and meditate on these verses.
title: Introduction

text: - personal reflection:
title: Introduction

text: Compare your local church with these 3 images.
title: Introduction

text: Are the characteristics highlighted by Paul present?
title: Introduction

text: Ask the Holy Spirit to show you what you can do to make your church truly a body and a family!
title: Introduction

text: - towards others:
title: Introduction

text: Examine your heart to see if your brothers and sisters at church have truly become your parents,
title: Introduction

text: as in your natural family.
